articles.title: Champions League draw: Mourinho’s quest for number 16 begins against Inter, Arsenal and Leipzig
articles.standfirst: Breaking down Real Madrid’s eight Champions League opponents
articles.summary: Breaking down Real Madrid’s eight Champions League opponents
articles.body:
R eal Madrid already know who they will face on their European road to the Sixteenth . The draw held today in Monaco handed the Whites a total of eight opponents for the 2026/27 Champions League league phase , four of them at the Santiago Bernabéu and four others away from home.

The competition also carries a special added incentive on the bench. José Mourinho faces his first Champions League of this second spell with an old unfinished score to settle: the Big Eared trophy eluded him in his first stint at Real Madrid, when he reached three consecutive semifinals without making the final . The Portuguese coach, who has lifted the trophy with other clubs, is now looking to settle that debt and return Madrid to the summit of a tournament the club considers its natural habitat.

Real Madrid's Champions League opponents

The draw was decided with the 36 participants split into four pots according to the UEFA coefficient, so that each team faces two opponents from each pot, one at home and one away. Madrid, placed in the first pot, could not be drawn against other Spanish clubs nor face more than two teams from the same country . The dates and kick-off times for each matchday will be announced over the weekend.

When does Real Madrid play in the Champions League?

Although Real Madrid already knows the names of its first eight opponents and knows which ones it will play against at the Santiago Bernabéu and which ones it will have to visit, there is still no schedule . UEFA will make it public over the weekend, and that will be the time to book tickets for the away matches and seats for the clashes at the Whites' home ground.

The format maintains the structure introduced in previous editions. The 36 teams share a single standings table: the top eight advance directly to the round of 16, while those placed between ninth and twenty-fourth play an intermediate two-legged round . The rest are eliminated, with no Europa League safety net. From the round of 16 onward, the tournament returns to its traditional knockout format through to the final, which this season will be played in its own city, on June 5, 2027 at the Metropolitano stadium.

Old acquaintances, rematches and a debut

The most storied clash will undoubtedly be that with Inter . The two giants have faced each other 19 times throughout history, with Madrid holding the upper hand (ten victories), although the Italians retain a painful episode for Madridismo. They were the executioners in the 1964 final , one of the few finals the club has lost. The reunion also has a special flavor for Mourinho , who won his second Champions League precisely with Inter , in 2010 and on the pitch at the Bernabéu . Recent meetings, however, have smiled on Madrid, who came out on top in both group-stage encounters in 2021/22.

More recent and tinged with revenge is the meeting with Arsenal . The Gunners eliminated Madrid in the quarter-finals of 2024/25 with a convincing 5-1 aggregate scoreline (3-0 at the Emirates, with a Declan Rice brace, and 2-1 at the Bernabéu), in one of the most bitter nights from two seasons ago. Los Blancos, now under Mourinho, will have the chance to make amends for that drubbing.

Roma also falls into the category of familiar old foes. The two teams have crossed paths repeatedly in the present century, always in the top competition, with their last meeting coming in the 2015/16 round of 16 , settled in Madrid's favor. Something similar applies to PSV and Shakhtar Donetsk , recent group-stage opponents against whom the club in white usually comes out on top, although the Ukrainian side — which will play its home matches at Stamford Bridge — has already pulled off a surprise or two, such as the 3-2 win it inflicted at Valdebebas in 2020/21.

Special mention goes to RB Leipzig , whom Madrid already faced in the group stage of 2022/23, and who now reappear with added intrigue: from their ranks comes the most expensive signing in the club's history, Yan Diomande . The list is completed by two exotic opponents: AEK Athens , a very rare matchup, and Austria's LASK , a completely new opponent in the club's European history. Two almost or entirely unprecedented scenarios for a Madrid side that, as always, starts with the status of favorite in its eternal pursuit of the Sixteenth.

articles.title: Blockbuster draw! Defending champions PSG set for epic clashes with Manchester City and Barcelona
articles.standfirst: Will they be able to dethrone the champion?
articles.summary: Will they be able to dethrone the champion?
articles.body:
Two-time defending champion Paris Saint-Germain will host Manchester City and travel to Barcelona in the Champions League main phase this season, after the 36-team draw was made Thursday.

PSG has won three straight visits to Barcelona — including a 2-1 win in the league phase last October — since imploding in the famous 6-1 loss in March 2017 that is known as the “ Remontada ” game.

The French champion again plays Aston Villa , after a Super Cup win this month, and goes to Champions League newcomer Como, coached by Cesc Fabregas , in an eight-game slate that starts in two weeks' time.

Real Madrid will host Inter Milan and make two trips to London, at Arsenal and against Shakhtar Donetsk . Ukraine’s champion is playing home games at Stamford Bridge, where Madrid's returning coach José Mourinho was beloved by Chelsea fans in a pair of title-winning spells there.

Barcelona will host two English clubs — Man City and Europa League winner Villa — plus its former player Fabregas with Como. A long trip to Azerbaijan awaits to face debutant Sabah in Baku.

Arsenal, the beaten finalist last year, will host Madrid, Borussia Dortmund and Sabah , and travel to Bayern Munich.

Bayern got a second English opponent, with a trip to Manchester United, plus two Norwegian opponents, hosting Bodø/Glimt and visiting Viking. Bayern also will go to Atletico Madrid whose Metropolitano Stadium will host the final next May.

Liverpool got trips to Inter Milan and Fenerbahce in what looked one of the more favorable slates of eight games. Atletico will again come to Anfield where Liverpool won 3-2 last September.

Atletico also will play both Norwegian teams and is one of four teams heading inside the Arctic Circle to play on Bodø/Glimt ’s artificial turf. Dortmund, Lille and newcomer LASK also will travel to the remote fishing town, and one team must make the trip in January.

Sabah also will host Dortmund, Napoli and Slavia Prague . Fans also have two long trips from Azerbaijan to England to face Arsenal and Man United.

Como has a second trip to Spain, to play Real Betis as well as Barcelona, and will welcome PSG and Man United to its picture-postcard lakeside stadium home.

Four debutants in Champions League draw

Four newcomers will debut in this Champions League edition: Como from Italy, coached by Cesc Fabregas; LASK of Austria; Viking from Norway; and Azerbaijani champion Sabah , which was founded only in 2017.

Sabah coach Valdas Dambrauskas is already making headlines for his curious origin story in soccer. The money he won as a young contestant on TV quiz show “ Who Wants to be a Millionaire ” in his native Lithuania funded a trip to study coaching in England.

Another first this season is an African coach taking his team into the main phase. Former Manchester City and Barcelona star Yaya Touré guided Slovakian champion Slovan Bratislava through its qualifying playoff Wednesday. Slovan will visit PSG and host Inter Milan .

Champions League draw details

UEFA’s draw software allocated eight opponents to each team — four home games, four away — with two opponents taken from each seeding pot. Seeding was decided by ranking a team's European results over the past five years. Teams could not be paired with an opponent from their own country.

The first round of games is played Sept. 8-10 with the first six rounds played through December. The league phase resumes in January with the eighth and final round on Jan. 27 .

The top eight teams in the final standings go direct to the round of 16 in March. Teams placed ninth to 24th enter the knockout playoffs in February to decide the other eight teams in the round of 16. Teams placed 25th to 36th are eliminated .

The 36 teams will share prize money of about 2.5 billion euros ($2.9 billion).

articles.title: Real Madrid and Barcelona: Who came out better after the 2026/27 Champions League draw?
articles.standfirst: The road to one of Europe’s biggest titles is beginning to take shape, and the two Spanish giants will not face the same challenge.
articles.summary: The road to one of Europe’s biggest titles is beginning to take shape, and the two Spanish giants will not face the same challenge.
articles.body:
The 2026 World Cup is now part of the past, but international soccer has a new story waiting to be written. This time, the spotlight returns to the clubs, with the Champions League beginning to reveal some of the matchups that could shape the season.

Real Madrid and Barcelona now know the eight teams they will face in the league phase of the 2026/27 edition , following Thursday’s draw in Monaco. And while it is still far too early to talk about favorites, simply looking at the names on their respective schedules reveals a difference that immediately stands out.

While one team will have to prepare to host Inter and travel to Arsenal, the other will face Manchester City, PSG and a difficult trip to Galatasaray .

The question, then, almost asks itself: who got the easier path?

Real Madrid already know their eight opponents

The Merengue side, led by José Mourinho , will play four matches at home and four away during this opening stage of the Champions League.

At home, they will face Inter, PSV, RB Leipzig and LASK . The matchup against the Italian side stands out as the biggest challenge of the four, although playing in front of their own fans could give Real Madrid an opportunity to collect valuable points from the start.

Things will look different on the road. Arsenal, Roma, Shakhtar Donetsk and AEK Athens will be their away opponents, with the trip to face the English side emerging as one of the matches likely to attract the most attention.

Barcelona have several big nights ahead

Barcelona, meanwhile, will begin the competition with several opponents capable of immediately raising the difficulty of their schedule.

At home, they will welcome Manchester City, Aston Villa, Feyenoord and Como . Among those matches, the clash with Pep Guardiola’s side stands out as one of the biggest attractions of the league phase.

Hansi Flick’s team will travel to face PSG, Sporting CP, Galatasaray and Sabah . And one match inevitably stands above the rest: their trip to Paris to take on the reigning European champions.

The matchup will also have an added layer of intrigue, as the two teams will meet again after their clash last season.

So, when it comes to who received the easier path, Real Madrid appear to have been handed a slightly more favorable route than Barcelona .

However, the draw is only the starting point. The real answer will come once the ball starts rolling and each opponent stops being just a name on a schedule and becomes a test capable of shaping the course of an entire season.

articles.title: Champions 26-27 schedule: match times for Real Madrid and Barcelona
articles.standfirst: UEFA published this Saturday all the schedules for the eight matchdays
articles.summary: UEFA published this Saturday all the schedules for the eight matchdays
articles.body:
UEFA published this Saturday the schedules for the eight matchdays of the Champions League league phase. In other words, the five Spanish teams ( Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atlético, Villarreal and Betis ) already know when and against whom they will play in each of the matchdays.

Thus, Real Madrid will make their debut against Inter at home (21:00) on Tuesday, September 8, Barcelona against Feyenoord also at home (18:45) on Wednesday, September 9, Atlético will visit Anfield (21:00) on Wednesday, September 9, Villarreal will play against Dortmund away (21:00) on Tuesday, September 8, and Betis against Lille away from home (21:00) on Tuesday, September 8.

After the draw held last Thursday, in which each team learned who their eight opponents would be, it remained to find out the times and dates on which they will face each of them. The matchday dates, which were already known, are as follows:

Matchday 1: September 8–10, 2026

Matchday 2: October 13/14, 2026

Matchday 3: October 20/21, 2026

Matchday 4: November 3/4, 2026

Matchday 5: November 24/25, 2026

Matchday 6: 8/9 December 2026

Matchday 7: January 19/20, 2027

Matchday 8: January 27, 2027

Playoff dates and matchups

As in previous years, the top eight teams in the league phase will qualify directly for the round of 16. The teams placed between ninth and twenty-fourth will play a playoff from which the other eight round-of-16 qualifiers will emerge. This playoff will be played on February 16/17 (the first-leg matches) and February 23/24 (the second-leg matches) in 2027.

Round of 16: March 9/10 and 16/17, 2027

Quarter-finals: April 6/7 and 13/14, 2027

Semi-finals: April 27/28 and May 4/5, 2027
